extra.message: Passwords are hashed with a single unsalted MD5 operation. Its negligible work factor and lack of salt allow efficient offline dictionary and rainbow-table attacks after password hashes are obtained.

RedisStorage explicitly creates the session cookie with httponly=False. Client-side JavaScript, including injected scripts through the stored XSS vulnerabilities, can read and exfiltrate the session identifier.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without HttpOnly Flag

extra.message: The session storage is created without enabling the Secure cookie attribute. The application is configured and documented for plain HTTP, allowing session identifiers to be transmitted over an unencrypted connection.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without Secure Attribute

extra.message: Successful authentication adds user_id to the existing session without invalidating or rotating its identifier. An attacker who fixes or obtains that identifier before login can reuse the authenticated session.

POST /students/ creates a database record without calling get_auth_user() or using the authorize decorator. Although the form is hidden from unauthenticated users, any remote caller can submit the POST request directly.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: POST /courses/ creates courses without server-side authentication or an administrator check. The template exposes this operation only to administrators, but an unauthenticated or non-administrator caller can invoke it directly.

POST /students/{student_id}/evaluate/{course_id} inserts grades without authentication or an administrator check. The UI presents grading only to administrators, but any remote caller can submit valid student, course, and points values directly.

The login handler checks every submitted credential pair without any rate limit, retry delay, account lockout, or equivalent attempt restriction. Remote attackers can perform unlimited online password-guessing attempts.
